title: Fluorescence-guided pelvic lymphadenectomy in prostate cancer: Restrospective analysis of diagnostic accuracy and oncologic outcomes
summary: We will retrospectively analyse diagnostic accuracy as well as oncological follow-up data of prostate cancer patients who underwent lymph node dissection under fluorescence guidance. We will compare these data with data from patients who underwent lymph node dissection under magnetometer guidance as well as from patients who underwent standard lymph node dissection. Analysis will take place retrospectively of data routinely collected at the clinic as well as at the prostate cancer center Oldenburg, Germany.

interventions.name: prostate cancer patients who underwent radical prostatectomy and fluorescence-guided pelvic lymphadenectomy; retrospective collection of data on diagnostic accuracy of lymph node marking with reference to extended pelvic lymphadenectomy from histopathology reports as well as collection of oncologic
prostate cancer patients who underwent radical prostatectomy and Magnetometer-guided pelvic lymphadenectomy; retrospective data collection as in arm 1
prostate cancer patients who underwent radical prostatectomy and extended pelvic lymphadenectomy; retrospective data collection as in arm 1

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Prostate cancer patients who underwent radical prostatectomy and fluorescence- or magnetometer-guided pelvic lymphadenectomy in combination with risk-adjusted extended pelvic lymphadenectomy or risk-adjusted pelvic lymphadenectomy alone at the University Hospital for Urology, Klinikum Oldenburg, Germany, between 01.02.2022 and 05.02.2025.
Exclusion criteria:
- patients with prior prostate surgery or with anti-hormonal treatment before radical prostatectomy
- cases with incomplete data
- patients unable to consent
